newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB down further on Oftel, cable news.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB down further on Oftel, cable news.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc extended their early decline by early afternoon Wednesday in reaction to yesterday's cable merger involving Cable & Wireless Plc and a negative ruling from telecoms regulator Oftel.
BSkyB shares, which set a record high of 698p on October 21, were down 32-1/2p at 646 by 1323 GMT in active trade of 4.3 million shares.
Analysts said the stock was probably due a correction after its heady rise in the past four months, which carried it up from 420p in mid June.

"It had got well ahead of itself," said Jason Crisp, analyst at SocGen, "the recent run was based on very flimsy hopes and didn't take account of any of the risks and difficulties that the company may face."
"It is doing very well but doesn't deserve its sky-high rating."

Earlier, Oftel issued a provisional order against a promotion between BSkyB and British Telecom, down 6-1/2p at 347-1/2, while the merger between C&W's Mercury unit and three cable operators threatened to increase competition with BSkyB.
